threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, touchpoints, and overall pilot plan.

messages.text: Kicking off the Cross-Channel Customer Feedback Improvement Pilot for the next 30 days. The goal is to design and run a focused pilot that captures, routes, and acts on feedback across our digital, support, membership, insurance, and on-site visit channels, using only our existing tools. I will own the overall coordination and reporting. For scope, my initial proposal for T1 is to include: digital (website forms, email, social), ICT help desk tickets, membership interactions, insurance complaints, and cellar visits. I will draft the first version of the process map and RACI in A1 today so we can all react. For timing, I suggest we treat the next 30 days as the full pilot window, with T11 covering the run and daily capture. Before we lock this in, I need each of you to confirm which touchpoints you can realistically include without disrupting your core work too much.

From the ICT help desk side, I can include all tickets where customers contact us via phone, email, or the portal. For T1, I will list: inbound calls, email inbox, and the self-service form as separate touchpoints, with our ticketing tool as the system owner. One question: do we also want to capture feedback that comes in as side comments on purely technical issues, or only when the customer explicitly says they have feedback or a complaint about service or products

On membership, I can bring in feedback from member emails, phone calls, and in-person conversations at the counter. For T1, I will map: membership email inbox, outbound campaigns that get replies, and front-desk interactions. I am slightly worried about the 30-day window if we also add proactive outreach, but for now I can commit to including all inbound membership contacts and any feedback we get during routine calls.

From insurance, I suggest we include all formal complaints and any written dissatisfaction that reaches us via email or letters. For T1, I will document: complaint emails, letters, and any complaint forms we receive via the website. I can also flag when something is borderline between a question and a complaint so we can see how that behaves in the pilot. No changes to coverage or terms on our side, just how we classify and route.

For the cellar, I can include feedback from guided tours and tastings. To keep disruption low during peak hours, I propose we only collect structured feedback at the end of each tour, not during production tasks. I will work on T6 and A3 so that the checklist is short enough to complete in a couple of minutes. For T1, I will list: guided tours, tastings at the cellar door, and any written notes visitors leave in the guest book.

On the help desk question: for the pilot, I would like us to capture both explicit feedback and side comments, as long as they relate to the customer experience or our services. We can tag them differently later once T2 is ready. This will give us a better view of what customers say in passing. We just need to make sure the intake script in T3 does not make calls too long.

Understood. I will treat side comments as in scope for the pilot and mark them clearly in the ticket so they can be tagged later once A2 is available. For T3, I will keep the script concise and test it on a few recent tickets to see if call duration changes noticeably.

On proactive outreach: for the first 30 days, I suggest we limit membership to feedback that comes up naturally in existing interactions. Once we see the load from the pilot, we can add a small proactive survey as part of T4. That should help us stay within the constraint of minimal disruption.

Agree on keeping membership proactive outreach out of the initial 30-day scope and focusing on feedback that arises in normal interactions. We can still design the proactive process in T4 so it is ready if we extend the pilot.

One more point from insurance: when we map T1, I will also note which complaints are already coded in our existing system so that later, for T7, we can align those codes with the new taxonomy in A2. That should reduce rework when we reclassify historical complaints.

For cellar visits, to respect the constraint on peak production hours, I propose we only run the checklist during tours that start outside the main bottling and racking windows. I will mark those time windows in A1 so everyone sees when cellar feedback is expected to be lower.
That works for me. Please add those time windows into the process map in A1 once I share the draft, so we can show that cellar feedback is intentionally limited during peak operations.

On the 30-day timeline and milestones: I propose we treat days 1 to 5 as setup and mapping (T1, T2, T3, T4, T6, T7, T9), days 6 to 27 as the active pilot run (T11), and days 28 to 30 for evaluation and reporting (T12, A8). We will also do short async check-ins in this channel to share daily volumes and blockers. Any strong objections to this structure
No objection from membership. The only thing I will watch is training time for T10. If we keep the scripts and checklist simple, I can fit short sessions into that first week.

Works for help desk as well. I will need at least two days in the first week to test and adjust the intake script for T3 before we train everyone in T10, but that still fits in your day 1 to 5 window.
Insurance is fine with that structure. It gives enough time to complete the mapping for T7 and to reclassify a small sample of historical complaints before the main pilot run starts.

From the cellar side, the timeline is acceptable as long as we avoid scheduling training during harvest-related peak days. I will share a quick note with the days that are most sensitive so we can plan T10 around them.

Summarising where we are: for scope, we will include digital channels, ICT help desk tickets, membership contacts, insurance complaints, and cellar visits, with cellar feedback limited to non-peak tours. For timing, we will run a 30-day pilot with days 1 to 5 for setup and training, days 6 to 27 for the active run, and days 28 to 30 for evaluation and reporting. I will reflect this in A1 and T11. Unless anyone objects by end of day, I will treat this as confirmed and move ahead.

threads.thread_goal: Define and finalise the unified feedback taxonomy and routing rules.

messages.text: I have uploaded a first draft of the unified feedback taxonomy into A2 for T2. It currently has 14 top-level categories, grouped roughly into: product quality, service quality, digital experience, membership, insurance, cellar visit, billing, and a few others. Each category has example phrases to help tagging. For routing, I also sketched initial rules in A2 that map categories to owners and to the shared log in A5. Please review with your lens and comment on any gaps, overlaps, or routing issues you see, especially where categories might cross teams.

Looking at A2 from the help desk side, I see a lot of tickets that mix digital experience and service quality. For example, a customer might say the portal is confusing and also that the person on the phone was very helpful. In A2, should we tag both categories for the same feedback item, or pick the main one only I am asking because in A5 we will need a clear rule so that we do not double count.

From membership, the categories for membership benefits and communication look good in A2, but I am missing a clear place for feedback about events and tastings that are part of the membership program. Right now they could fall under membership or cellar visit. Maybe we need a subcategory that is shared between those two so routing to A5 is consistent.

On the insurance side, the complaint categories in A2 align broadly with our existing codes, but I see two areas where we might need more detail: claim handling time and clarity of policy wording. Both are currently under a single insurance service category. For T7, it would help if we split them so that when we reclassify historical complaints, we can see patterns more clearly.

For cellar visits, A2 has a single cellar visit category with subcategories for tour, tasting, and safety. That is a good start, but I suggest we add a subcategory for logistics, such as parking and signage. Those issues often come up and they are not really about the wine or the guide. Routing-wise, I assume cellar visit feedback still goes to me first, even if the root cause is something like parking.

On multi-topic feedback: for the pilot, I propose we allow up to two tags per feedback item in A5. That way, if a customer mentions both portal usability and phone support, we can tag both digital experience and service quality. In A5, we will treat the feedback as a single record with multiple tags, and in the dashboard we can count by tag, not by record, when needed. Does that sound workable for help desk workflows
Yes, limiting to two tags per feedback item is manageable. I will add a short note into the draft help desk script in A4 so agents know they can select up to two categories when logging into A5.

Good point on events and tastings that are part of membership. I suggest we add a shared subcategory called member events under both membership and cellar visit in A2, with a routing rule that sends it first to membership for coordination, but with cellar copied when the feedback is about the on-site experience. That way A5 will show a consistent tag, and we can still see which team is primary.

Shared member events as a subcategory works for me. For routing, I am fine being the first owner in A5, as long as we have a clear note that cellar is responsible for operational fixes on-site. I can then coordinate communication back to the member.

Agreed on the shared member events subcategory. If A5 flags those items to both membership and cellar, I can review anything related to the visit logistics or wine experience and feed back to membership on what we can change operationally.

On insurance, I will split the insurance service category in A2 into at least two subcategories: claim handling time and clarity of policy wording. For T7, that should make the mapping from your existing codes more straightforward. For routing, both will still go to insurance first in A5, but we can add an escalation rule for policy wording issues that might need legal review.

That split will help a lot. For T7, I will take a sample of at least ten historical complaints and reclassify them using the updated A2, then share any patterns I see so we can adjust if needed before we lock the taxonomy.

Adding a logistics subcategory under cellar visit makes sense. I will add that to A2 and set the routing so that cellar is the first owner in A5, but with a note that some actions might involve facilities or signage teams outside this group. For the pilot, we can still log them and track resolution time even if another team executes the fix.
Perfect. I will make sure cellar staff using the checklist in A3 know how to distinguish between tour, tasting, safety, and logistics so that when we transfer data into A5, the tags match A2.

On routing rules overall, here is what I propose for the pilot: membership-related categories route to membership as primary owner, with help desk or cellar copied when relevant; insurance categories route to insurance; digital experience issues route to help desk as primary, with BI copied for analysis; cellar visit categories route to cellar; and any data privacy concerns route to help desk to log and then to the data protection officer. All items go into A5 with a clear owner and due date. Please flag if any of these default routes would cause issues in your day-to-day work.

Routing digital experience issues to help desk as primary is fine. I will add a short field in the intake script in A4 so agents can see the default owner and do not have to guess. For data privacy concerns, I will log them under a specific category in A2 so they are easy to filter in A5.

Membership routing looks good. The only nuance is that some membership feedback is actually about digital channels, like trouble logging into the member area. In those cases, I will still log it under the digital experience category in A2 and route to help desk in A5, while keeping visibility on the membership side.

Insurance routing is fine. For complaints that touch both insurance and membership, for example when a member is unhappy about how a claim affects their benefits, I will tag both insurance and membership categories in A2 and set membership as copied in A5 so we can coordinate the response.

Thanks for all the input. I will now update A2 with the agreed changes: multi-tagging up to two categories, shared member events subcategory, split insurance service into claim handling time and policy wording, and add cellar logistics. I will also finalise the routing rules in A5 as discussed. Once I post the updated version, I will consider the taxonomy and routing rules approved for the pilot unless there are blocking comments.

threads.thread_goal: Align on frontline scripts, checklists, and training approach.

messages.text: I have drafted the first version of the help desk intake script and shared it in A4 for T3. It covers: greeting, a short explanation that we are running a feedback pilot, a brief data privacy note, and a few key questions to capture structured feedback and tags for A5. The script is designed to add no more than one minute to a normal call. I would appreciate your feedback on tone, length, and any missing points, especially where it touches membership, insurance, or cellar topics.

Thanks for sharing the script. From a membership perspective, the tone feels friendly and clear. I would suggest adding one short line that invites members to share feedback about their overall membership experience, not just the immediate issue. That will help T4 when we design the proactive membership process, because we will already have some structured examples.

Looking at A4 with an insurance lens, the data privacy note is a bit generic. Since we will also rely on A7 and T9, I recommend we reference that feedback will be stored in line with our existing data protection rules and that customers can ask for more details. I will check with the person responsible for compliance to make sure the wording is acceptable before we finalise.

For cellar-related calls, the script in A4 works, but I would keep the questions about on-site visits very short. Many visitors call while they are on the road. Maybe we can ask just one or two questions and then, if needed, invite them to share more feedback during the cellar visit using the checklist in A3.

From a BI standpoint, the structure in A4 is good. For T3, I would only add a quick internal reminder for agents to capture the category tags based on A2 and to log everything into A5. That will make it easier to validate the dashboard later for T5.

I can add a short line inviting members to share feedback about their overall membership experience, phrased so it does not feel like a survey. I will update A4 accordingly and mark that part as optional if the call is already long.

On the privacy note, I will adjust the wording in A4 to say that feedback is stored according to our existing data protection rules and that more details are available on request. I will rely on you and the compliance contact to confirm that this matches A7 and T9 before we roll it out.

Good point on short questions for on-site visits. I will keep the cellar-related part of the script to one or two questions and then direct visitors to the on-site checklist in A3 when they arrive, so we do not overload the call.

On the cellar side, I have a draft of the visit feedback checklist in A3 for T6. It covers four sections: overall visit experience, tasting, safety, and logistics. Each section has a few quick rating items and one open comment field. The format is one page so it can be used on paper or tablet. I would like your input on whether the questions are clear enough for visitors and whether we should add anything specific for members versus non-members.

The checklist in A3 looks clear. For members, maybe we can add a small tick box that indicates whether the visitor is a member, plus one optional question about how the visit fits their expectations from the membership program. That will help T4 and T10 when we explain the value of the program during training.

From a data perspective, the four sections in A3 map nicely to the categories in A2. For T6, the only thing I would add is a small field at the top for date and tour time, so we can later check if certain time slots or peak days correlate with different feedback patterns.

I will add a member tick box and a short optional question about membership expectations to A3. It should not add much time for visitors to complete, and it will help us distinguish between member and non-member feedback in the pilot.
Good idea on date and tour time. I will add those fields at the top of A3 so that when we hand completed checklists to BI for A6, you can analyse patterns by time slot.

Given the scripts and checklist are shaping up, we should align on T10, the training approach. My suggestion is: short 30-minute sessions for each team, focusing on why we are running the pilot, how to use A4 and A3, and how to log into A5. We can run one session for help desk, one for membership, one for insurance, and a short briefing for cellar staff at the start of a shift. Does that sound realistic for everyone

For help desk, a 30-minute session is fine. I can walk through the script in A4, show how to pick categories from A2, and demonstrate logging into A5. I would prefer to schedule it outside peak call hours, maybe early afternoon.

Insurance can also do a 30-minute session. I will use it to explain how the new categories in A2 map to our existing codes for T7 and how to handle any questions about data protection using A7 and T9.

For cellar staff, we might need two shorter briefings of about 15 minutes each, one at the start of the morning shift and one in the afternoon, to avoid disrupting tours. I can cover how to use A3 and when to hand completed checklists over so they can be logged into A5.
I can join the sessions to give a quick overview of the pilot goals and how the data will feed into A6 and the final report in A8. That should help frontline staff see how their input will be used.

Given the feedback and updates, I propose we consider the help desk script in A4 and the membership parts of it ready for pilot use, once the privacy wording is confirmed against A7 and T9. For membership-specific conversations, I will also prepare a short written guide that aligns with A4 so we are consistent across channels.

On the cellar checklist, with the latest tweaks in A3, I am comfortable using it during visits that start outside peak production hours. We will hand it out at the end of the tour, collect it before visitors leave, and pass it to BI at the end of each day. That will be our standard use during the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Set up KPI tracking, data protection rules, and dashboard expectations.

messages.text: I have drafted a list of pilot KPIs and a data handling proposal for T5 and T9. For KPIs, I suggest we track: total feedback volume by channel, category mix based on A2, average time to first response, average time to resolution, and the share of feedback that leads to a concrete action. The data model behind A6 will pull from A5 and our existing systems. For data protection, I have outlined access levels and retention rules in A7, aligned with our current policies. Please review and let me know if these KPIs and rules are workable from your side.

From help desk, the KPIs look reasonable. The only concern is measuring time to first response, since for calls it is immediate. Maybe we can treat call-based feedback as having zero delay and focus that metric more on email and written channels. On data access in A7, I want to confirm that frontline agents will only see feedback they need for their work, not everything in A6.

For membership, I like the idea of tracking the share of feedback that leads to an action. Could we also have a simple sentiment indicator in A6, even if it is just positive, neutral, negative based on tags or a quick manual rating That would help when we report back to marketing and membership leadership.

On insurance, the KPIs are fine, but we should be careful with how we store and access complaint details. In A7 and T9, I see that access to detailed complaint text is limited to a small group. I support that. For the pilot, I suggest we anonymise names in A6 where possible and only keep identifiers in our core system.

For cellar visits, tracking volume and category mix is straightforward. Time to resolution might be trickier, because some actions, like changing signage, depend on other teams. Maybe for cellar we can also track a simpler metric, such as the share of cellar feedback that gets at least an acknowledgement back to the visitor or member.

On time to first response, I agree that calls can be treated as immediate. In A6, I will calculate that KPI only for channels where there is a delay, such as email, web forms, and letters. For access, A7 defines that frontline agents see only feedback records they are responsible for in A5, while aggregated views in A6 will be available to managers and BI. Does that address your concern
Yes, that works. As long as agents only see their own or team-related items in A5 and not all detailed records in A6, we are fine from my side.

We can add a simple sentiment field to A5 and propagate it into A6. For the pilot, I suggest we keep it manual: the person logging the feedback selects positive, neutral, or negative based on the overall tone. That will give us a basic sentiment view without adding complex tooling.
Manual sentiment tagging is fine. I will include a short explanation in the membership training for T10 so people know how to choose between the three options consistently.

On anonymisation, I agree. In A6, we will store only a feedback ID, date, channel, category, sentiment, and timing metrics. Names and contact details will stay in the source systems. A7 and T9 will document that only a small group, including insurance and BI, can access full complaint text when needed.

That setup works for insurance. I will double-check with the compliance contact that the anonymisation approach in A6 and the access rules in A7 and T9 are in line with our obligations, and I will flag any required tweaks.

For cellar, we can add an extra KPI: share of cellar feedback that receives an acknowledgement or follow-up within a set time, for example five working days. We will track that in A5 and surface it in A6. For items that depend on other teams, we can still count the acknowledgement even if the fix takes longer.
That is workable. I will make sure cellar staff know to log when they have acknowledged feedback so that A5 has the right data for that KPI.

On T9, I have one practical question: for help desk tickets that contain both technical details and feedback, do we need to separate the feedback text into a different field for A6, or is it enough to tag the ticket and rely on the tag only I want to avoid copying text around if possible.

For the pilot, tagging is enough. We do not need to copy the feedback text into A6. We will just pull the ticket ID, tags, and timing fields. That keeps T9 simpler and reduces the risk of exposing unnecessary personal data.

Given the discussion, I am comfortable with the KPI set you proposed, plus the sentiment and cellar acknowledgement metrics. From membership, I do not see any blockers to using these as our core pilot KPIs.
Same from insurance. As long as the anonymisation and access rules in A7 and T9 are applied as described, I am fine with the KPI list and the way A6 will be populated.

To wrap this up: we will track the following core KPIs in A6 for the pilot: feedback volume by channel, category mix, time to first response for non-call channels, time to resolution, share of feedback leading to an action, sentiment, and share of cellar feedback acknowledged within five working days. Data will be logged in A5 and anonymised in A6, with access rules and retention documented in A7 and T9. Unless there are objections, I will treat these KPIs and data rules as approved and proceed with T5 and T9.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on next steps and roadmap.

messages.text: We have completed the 30-day pilot, and I have shared the preliminary results in A8, based on data from A6 and logs in A5 for T11 and T12. Highlights: we captured 420 feedback items across all channels, with the largest share from help desk and membership. Average time to first response for email and web forms was under one working day, and average time to resolution was just under five working days. About 35 percent of feedback items led to a concrete action. I would like your reactions and any key observations from your teams before we decide whether to extend, scale, or stop the pilot.

From the help desk side, agents adapted to the script in A4 quite well after the first week. We saw a noticeable increase in tagged feedback in A5, especially around digital experience. The main friction was remembering to apply sentiment and a second tag when needed, but that improved with reminders. I think the process is workable if we keep the script stable and maybe add a quick refresher in future training.

Membership saw good engagement, especially from members who appreciated being asked for feedback. In A6, I noticed that membership-related feedback skewed more positive than neutral or negative, which is useful for our messaging. The main challenge was logging in A5 after in-person conversations; sometimes notes were delayed until the end of the day. If we continue, I would like to streamline that step, maybe with a simple mobile-friendly form.

On insurance, the new categories in A2 and the mapping in T7 worked well. Reclassifying historical complaints helped us see that a significant portion of issues were about claim handling time. During the pilot, we also saw a small but clear cluster of policy wording concerns. The anonymisation approach in A6 and the access rules in A7 and T9 held up; I did not hear any concerns from compliance.

For cellar visits, the checklist in A3 was easy for visitors to complete, and staff could handle it without disrupting tours, especially with the time window limits we set. We collected fewer items than other channels, but they were very specific and actionable, for example about signage and tasting pacing. The acknowledgement KPI in A6 showed that we responded to most cellar feedback within a week, which feels acceptable.

Good to hear that the script in A4 settled in. In A8, I noted that digital experience feedback from help desk was one of the main sources of improvement ideas, especially around navigation and login flows. If we extend or scale, we might want to prioritise a few of those items with IT operations.

On membership logging delays, A8 shows that most membership feedback still made it into A5 on the same day, but there were some gaps. If we continue, I agree that a simpler capture method for in-person conversations would help. That might require some configuration work, so we would need to check with IT before committing.

Yes, I would not want to promise a new tool without IT input. For now, even a small tweak to the existing form layout could help. Overall, I see enough value in the membership insights in A6 and A8 to justify continuing in some form.

One more observation from insurance: using the unified taxonomy in A2 made it easier to discuss cross-team issues, for example when a complaint touched both insurance and membership. That shared language is something I would like to keep, even if we adjust the process later.

I also noticed that cellar feedback helped us spot small safety and logistics issues early, like slippery steps or unclear parking signs. Even with a modest volume, the impact felt high. I would support keeping the checklist in A3 as a standard part of tours, with some seasonal adjustments.

In terms of workload, the pilot added some effort for help desk, but it was manageable once people got used to A4 and A5. If we scale, I would suggest we keep the current scope and avoid adding more mandatory questions, otherwise call handling times might creep up.

From membership, I would lean towards extending and gradually scaling, rather than stopping. The pilot gave us a clearer view of what members value and where they struggle. If we stop now, we lose that ongoing signal. If we scale too fast, we risk overloading teams, so a phased approach seems safer.

I am in favour of extending and gradually scaling as well. For insurance, the pilot showed that the taxonomy and routing work, and the data in A6 is already useful for spotting trends. We just need to keep an eye on data protection as volumes grow, but A7 and T9 give us a good base.

From the cellar side, I would also support extending the pilot, at least for another cycle, and then deciding on a full rollout. The process fits into our routines now that staff are used to A3, and the insights are helpful for planning improvements around the visitor experience.

I do not see a strong reason to stop. The main risk is fatigue if we keep changing scripts. If we extend, I would recommend we keep A4 stable and only make small tweaks based on clear evidence from A8.

Based on A8 and your feedback, my proposal is to extend the pilot for another 30 days and start preparing for a broader rollout. During the extension, we would keep the current scope and tools, focus on stabilising scripts and checklists, and refine a small set of high-impact improvements identified in A8. After that, we can present a roadmap for scaling to leadership. Any strong objections to this direction
No objection from membership. Extending for another 30 days with the same scope and then proposing a phased rollout sounds like the right balance.
Insurance is aligned with that plan. I would just add that we should keep monitoring any regulatory changes that might affect A7 and T9 during the extension.
From the cellar side, I am comfortable with another 30 days under the same conditions, especially the time window limits for collecting feedback.
Help desk is on board as long as we keep A4 stable and do not add more mandatory questions during the extension.

Thanks all. Summarising: we agree to extend the pilot for another 30 days with the current scope and tools, focus on stabilising scripts and checklists, and prepare a roadmap for a phased rollout based on the insights in A8. I will update T11 and T12 accordingly and share a short plan for the extension phase.
